children: If Arbitration, the place where the arbitration is to be held is Edinburgh.
The Scottish Arbitration Rules apply, subject to the following:

Rule 31(2): After the words “tribunal specifies” insert the words “if any party fails to comply with such a direction, the tribunal may consider such a direction, the tribunal may consider such failure when awarding expenses under Rule 62”
Rule 34(1): At the start of this Rule, insert the words “Subject to the consent of the parties, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld”
Rule 37(2): After the words “admission of anything).” Insert the words “The tribunal may consider such delay when awarding expenses under Rule 62”
The following additional Rules will apply to any Arbitration:

(1) The Subcontractor agrees to participate in any dispute resolution involving the Contractor and the Employer under the Main Contract if the parties to that agreement request the participation of the Subcontractor in the dispute resolution and the dispute touches or concerns the Subcontract Works.

(2) The initiation of dispute resolution under the Main Contract shall automatically stay dispute resolution under this Subcontract of any matter related to the dispute under the Main Contract, except to the extent that the Contractor waives such stay.  The Subcontractor may by written notice require the Contractor to elect with 14 days whether to waive such stay or to seek to join the dispute under this Subcontract with a related dispute under the Main Contract. The Subcontractor agrees to take any steps necessary or required by the Contractor to join the resolution under this Subcontract of any dispute with the resolution of any related dispute under the Main Contract.  Further the Subcontractor shall be bound by any decision or award of a tribunal appointed under the Main Contract to the extent that it decides issues related to the dispute under this Subcontract and the Subcontractor has participated in the dispute resolution.
The person or organisation who will choose an arbitrator
• If the Parties cannot agree a choice; or
• If the arbitration procedure does not state who selects an arbitrator is The President of the Institution of Civil Engineers.

children: The {em:Subcontractor} will attend progress meetings weekly or as otherwise required by the {em:Contractor}'s site management. When attending such progress meetings the {em:Subcontractor} must provide a written report which outlines the progress of the {em:subcontract works} to date, the position with regard to material deliveries, details of outstanding information and any other matters which are considered should be raised in relation to the {em:subcontract works}.

children: The {em:Subcontractor} will not carry out any works which are additional to the {em:subcontract works} other than following the {em:Contractor}'s written instruction. Instructions will be cross referenced to the main contract where applicable. A compensation event does not arise and no payment will be made for any extra costs which the {em:Subcontractor} considers he is due which are not covered by such written instruction from the {em:Contractor}.

children.name: text
children: The {em:Contractor}'s project manager is the only person authorised to sign instructions to the {em:Subcontractor} for additional work. Any other signatories will be invalid.

children.name: text

The {em:Contractor} will not entertain any claims whatsoever, or make any payment for such claims, where these procedures are not adhered to.

children.name: text

children.name: text

children.name: text
children: The {em:Contractor}'s project manager's or site manager's signature on a daywork sheet must be confirmed and countersigned by the {em:Contractor}'s quantity surveyor. The {em:Contractor}'s quantity surveyor will only certify monies on a daywork basis if in his opinion the work cannot be valued by any other means under the {em:subcontract}.

children.name: text

children.name: text

children.name: text
children: The Contractor is committed to improving safety performance and standards in industry as part of Build UK.  The Contractor will require that a competent and qualified work force is employed on all of the Contractor's projects in accordance with Construction Leadership Council recommendations on Industry Card Schemes, which provides a consistent means of recognising that an individual has achieved the agreed standard of qualification and skill in the occupation they are working in. Sub-Contractors shall therefore comply with these requirements forthwith and shall demonstrate such compliance by providing evidence as is reasonably required by the Contractor in advance of working on site.

children.name: text
children: In any event the Sub-Contractor, his sub-sub-contractors and/or his operatives shall produce CSCS cards or recognised equivalent as detailed in the CLC (Construction Leadership Council) recommendations prior to commencing any work on site.  Failure to provide certificated CSCS (or equivalent) labour will render such labour inadmissible to site and the Sub-Contractor shall provide alternate certificated labour to comply with those obligations.

children.name: text
children: The {em:Subcontractor}, his Sub-sub-contractors and/or his operatives shall attend a safety induction briefing with a {em:Contractor} representative prior to working on site.  Inductions will be held at set times only, with late arrivals not being admitted entry to site until they have attended a subsequent induction.

children.name: text
children: The {em:Sub-Contractor} shall indemnify the {em:Contractor} against and from any Fee for Intervention (FFI) made pursuant to the Health and Safety (Fees) Regulations 2016 to the extent that the Sub-Contractor has contributed to the material breach giving rise to the FFI. Where the material breach could have been avoided by the Sub-Contractor then he shall be fully responsible for the FFI.

children.name: text
children: The {em:Subcontractor} provides the {em:Contractor} with a copy of all safety procedures, instructions, rules and regulations issued by the {em:Subcontractor} to his employees, servants and agents.

The {em:Subcontractor}, before the start of the {em:subcontract works}, and at such other times as the {em:Contractor} may require, submits to the {em:Contractor} for approval a risk assessment and method statement which indicates how the {em:subcontract works} are to be carried out in a safe manner. Approval by the {em:Contractor} of the {em:Subcontractor}'s statement does not in any way relieve the {em:Subcontractor} of any of his statutory obligations or obligations at common law or under the subcontract.

children.name: text
children: The {em:Contractor} considers health and safety to be of prime importance. As a means of improving the safety culture on site, the {em:Contractor} has instigated a “No Accident Behaviour” (NAB) scheme.  All subcontractors are required to commit to this culture of further improving attitudes towards safety by allowing their operatives the time to become involved in the processes forming part of this commitment.

children.name: text
children: The {em:Subcontractor} will attend the {em:Contractor} daily Site safety audit.

children.name: text
children: All the {em:Contractor}'s sites are hard hat, safety footwear and high visibility jacket (together the "Personal Protective Equipment" or "PPE") compliant sites. The {em:Subcontractor} will ensure that all his personnel who work on or visit the Site are provided with and wear at all times suitable PPE. The {em:Contractor} may remove from the Site anyone who fails to comply with this requirement. The {em:Subcontractor} has included for the provision of all necessary PPE in the Price.

children.name: text
children: During the course of the {em:works} in the main contract, regular safety meetings will be held and the {em:Subcontractor}'s designated safety representative will attend.  If the {em:Subcontractor}'s designated safety representative fails to attend such meetings on a regular basis a fine will be will be imposed.

children.name: text
children: The following acts are strictly prohibited on the Site (and on all of the {em:Contractor}'s sites):
• The use of radios, stereos, cassette recorders, mobile telephones etc;
• Use of caravans as hutment’s etc.
• Possession or use of narcotics; and
• Other restrictions unique to this Site as specified in the Subcontract Scope and/or Subcontract Site Information,

and the {em:Subcontractor} will not permit any of its operatives to commit any such prohibited act on the Site and will notify the {em:Contractor} if it becomes aware of any other party committing such prohibited act on the Site.

children.name: text
children: All operatives employed by the {em:Subcontractor} will attend an induction from the {em:Contractor} prior to being allowed to enter the Site. Inductions will be held daily {TimeInductionHeld}.

children.name: text
